items.claim: The row's left seam is drawn at the koh-amar of verse 21, but the discourse-imperative summons in the verse just before it is a stronger, undisclosed rival for this unit's true opening.
items.evidence: Jer.29.20 reads “Hear therefore Yahweh’s word, all you captives whom I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon” (web:Jer.29.20) — an addressee-shift imperative summoning the captives to a word that follows immediately, the same discourse-imperative shape that opens a fresh unit at Jer.10.1 elsewhere in the book. The row's device_notes cite the setumah at oshb:Jer.29.20 only as the preceding material's own close (WLC, single-witness, tier-3), and the disclosed rejected alternative weighs only whether verse 22's curse formula should split from verse 21 — it never weighs whether verse 20's own summons belongs forward, as this unit's true tier-1 opening, rather than backward as a coda. If verse 20 opens this unit, the row's own span starts one verse late and its disclosed rival is not the strongest one available.

items.claim: The row's boundaries, its handling of the nested letter frame, and its quotations all hold up against the underlying bytes.
items.evidence: The opening at verse 24 turns to a third named figure under a fresh commissioning (“Concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall speak, saying,” web:Jer.29.24, matching the full verse's oshb byte string), distinct in kind from the direct divine sentence naming Ahab and Zedekiah that closes just before it; the row correctly names Jeremiah as the commissioned speaker and Shemaiah's own letter as the differently-owned quoted medium inside it. The close at verse 29 stops short of the fresh word-event formula actually opening verse 30. The setumah at oshb:Jer.29.23 and petuchah at oshb:Jer.29.29 both check out against the mark inventory, and the defective spelling claimed for the Anathothite gentilic at verse 27 matches its byte-reviewed classification. Both English quotations are exact, full-verse matches to the staged WEB text.

items.claim: The verdict quotation is glossed in English well beyond the extent of the full Hebrew verse it cites, folding in clauses the row never actually splices.
items.evidence: The verdict sentence is the full verse לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֜ד עַל שְׁמַעְיָ֣ה הַנֶּחֱלָמִי֮ וְעַל זַרְעוֹ֒ לֹא יִהְיֶ֨ה ל֜וֹ אִ֣ישׁ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּתוֹךְ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא יִרְאֶ֥ה בַטּ֛וֹב אֲשֶׁר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה לְעַמִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי סָרָ֥ה דִבֶּ֖ר עַל יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.29.32) in which ‘Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring’ is only the first clause; the verse continues, in Hebrew the row never splices at all, into the clauses meaning ‘he will not have a man to dwell among this people’ and ‘he will not see the good that I do for my people.’ The row nonetheless splices only the shorter opening clause and labels that splice as matching the full three-clause English quotation “Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring. He will not have a man to dwell among this people. He won’t see the good that I will do to my people,” (web:Jer.29.32), so the English quotation reaches well past the Hebrew string it is paired with. This does not affect the word-event and mark disclosures earlier in the row, which check out against the inventory.

items.claim: The frame-seam flip, the word-event opening, and every quotation in the row are all correctly grounded.
items.evidence: The span opens on the hadavar-asher-hayah header at Jer.30.1, one of the book's eleven prose-sermon superscription sites, and the row's parent_collection correctly flips from the prior frame to the frame that opens exactly there. All four verses' Hebrew splices and English quotations cover the identical full-verse span on both sides (oshb/web:Jer.30.1 through Jer.30.4), and the row stops short of the fresh koh-amar that actually opens the next unit at Jer.30.5. The setumah at oshb:Jer.29.32 and petuchah at oshb:Jer.30.3 both check out against the mark inventory.

items.claim: The unit's own opening quotation, the koh-amar the row relies on as its seam warrant, is glossed in English only from partway through the Hebrew verse spliced beside it.
items.evidence: The row splices the full verse כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) but glosses it only as “We have heard a voice of trembling; a voice of fear, and not of peace.” (web:Jer.30.5), leaving the opening formula's own English equivalent, “For Yahweh says:”, unglossed even though it stands in the same staged WEB verse and the same Hebrew byte string the row cites as its unit-opening device. The remaining quotations in the row (verses 7, 8, 10, and 11) are all full-span matches, and the day-alas classification of the hoy at verse 7 and the closure-only role given the neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack at verse 8 both hold up.

items.claim: Both of the row's own load-bearing quotations, at its opening and its close, gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them.
items.evidence: At the opening, the row splices the full verse כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) but glosses only “Your hurt is incurable. Your wound is grievous.” (web:Jer.30.12), leaving the koh-amar clause itself, “For Yahweh says,”, unglossed. At the close, the row splices the full verse כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִדָּחָה֙ קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֔ךְ צִיּ֣וֹן הִ֔יא דֹּרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte) but glosses only its second half, “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’” (web:Jer.30.17), leaving “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” says Yahweh, unglossed. The verse-15 quotation is a full-span match, and the mark disclosures throughout check out.

items.claim: Both the row's opening quotation and its quotation of the actively-held closing verse gloss only part of the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them.
items.evidence: At the opening, the row splices the full verse כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי שָׁב֙ שְׁבוּת֙ אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו אֲרַחֵ֑ם וְנִבְנְתָ֥ה עִיר֙ עַל תִּלָּ֔הּ וְאַרְמ֖וֹן עַל מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ יֵשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte) but glosses only “Behold, I will reverse the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. The city will be built on its own hill, and the palace will be inhabited in its own place.” (web:Jer.30.18), leaving the koh-amar clause's own English equivalent, “Yahweh says:”, unglossed. At the close, the row splices the full verse בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte) but glosses only “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.” (web:Jer.31.1), leaving “At that time,” says Yahweh, unglossed — on precisely the verse the row itself holds open as a genuine seam question, where the full formula bears on whether the verse reads forward or back. The Jacob plene-spelling disclosure and the mark citations elsewhere in the row check out.

items.claim: Both of the unit's first two verses are glossed in English only from partway through the full Hebrew verse spliced beside them.
items.evidence: At verse 2, the row splices the full verse כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מָצָ֥א חֵן֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר עַ֖ם שְׂרִ֣ידֵי חָ֑רֶב הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte) — the unit's own opening koh-amar — but glosses only “The people who survive the sword found favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.” (web:Jer.31.2), leaving “Yahweh says,” unglossed. At verse 3, the row splices the full verse מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ עַל כֵּ֖ן מְשַׁכְתִּ֥יךְ חָֽסֶד (oshb:Jer.31.3, byte) but glosses only “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.” (web:Jer.31.3), leaving its own opening clause, “Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,”, unglossed. The verse-4 and verse-6 quotations are full-span matches, and the closing petuchah at oshb:Jer.31.6 checks out.
